title: Finite etale-local splitting descends through a surjective closed immersion
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], let $r:R\to Y$ be a surjective closed immersion [def-weil-surjective-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $U\subseteq Y$ be open. Put $U_R=r^{-1}(U)$ and $g:X\times_Y R\to R$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume an etale covering family $T_i\to U_R$ is given such that each $T_i\times_{U_R} g^{-1}(U_R)$ has a finite pairwise disjoint open covering $(W_{ij})_{j\in\operatorname{Fin}(n_i)}$, and each composite $W_{ij}\to T_i$ is a universal homeomorphism [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism]. Then there is an etale covering family $S_a\to U$ such that every $S_a\times_U f^{-1}(U)$ likewise has a finite pairwise disjoint open covering whose component maps to $S_a$ are universal homeomorphisms. The integers may be zero. There are no Noetherian, reduced, affine or density assumptions.

source.document: Stacks Project, etale-cohomology.tex and morphisms.tex; parent generic finite Noetherian splitting proof

proof.text: Apply the proved cover lifting and source comparison lemma to the etale cover in the hypothesis. For each new cover member obtain an old cover member and surjective closed immersions of both the cover objects and their pulled-back sources, satisfying the first-projection equation.

Apply the proved finite open partition transport lemma to the source comparison. It produces a disjoint open partition covering the new source, finite inclusions of its components, and surjective comparison maps from the old components. Compose the finite inclusions with the finite base change of f to see that each new component map is finite.

For a component a:W->V, write g:V->S for its new structural map and t:T->S for the cover comparison. The two projection equations identify a followed by g with the old component map followed by t. Both latter maps are universal homeomorphisms, so their composite is one. Surjectivity of a implies surjectivity of g. For any test pullback of g, pull back a to a surjective map a_prime; pasting squares shows a_prime followed by the tested g is a base change of a followed by g and is therefore injective. Lift two points through a_prime to deduce injectivity of the tested g. Thus g is universally injective; finiteness supplies integrality. Assemble IsUniversalHomeomorphism g and the transported partition. This is the private helper universalHomeomorphism_of_surjective_precomp and the final proof.

lean.statement:
theorem finite_splitting_descends_surjective_closedImmersion
    {X Y R : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite f]
    (r : R ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion r] [Surjective r] (U : Y.Opens)
    (h : ∃ 𝒯 : Cover.{u} etalePrecoverage (r ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme, ∀ i,
      ∃ (n : ℕ)
        (W : Fin n → (pullback (𝒯.f i) (pullback.snd f r ∣_ (r ⁻¹ᵁ U))).Opens),
        (⨆ j, W j) = ⊤ ∧ Pairwise (fun j k ↦ Disjoint (W j) (W k)) ∧
        ∀ j, IsUniversalHomeomorphism
          ((W j).ι ≫ pullback.fst (𝒯.f i) (pullback.snd f r ∣_ (r ⁻¹ᵁ U)))) :
    ∃ 𝒯 : Cover.{u} etalePrecoverage U.toScheme, ∀ i,
      ∃ (n : ℕ) (W : Fin n → (pullback (𝒯.f i) (f ∣_ U)).Opens),
        (⨆ j, W j) = ⊤ ∧ Pairwise (fun j k ↦ Disjoint (W j) (W k)) ∧
        ∀ j, IsUniversalHomeomorphism
          ((W j).ι ≫ pullback.fst (𝒯.f i) (f ∣_ U))
